title: RetroUI (neobrutalism/neobrutalism)
lede: A React and Tailwind library published under the name NeoBrutalism, now branded RetroUI.
summary: Component library whose banner mixes hard-shadowed display type with retro window frames.

evidence.note: Downloaded and inspected the README banner `public/banner.png` (1200 × 630). Licence read through the GitHub API. The live sites were not captured.

styles.note: The repository is published as a NeoBrutalism library, and its banner uses outlined blocks, hard shadows, and flat yellow fills.

context: The GitHub description reads “A NeoBrutalism styled React + TailwindCSS UI library”. The README heading is “Retro UI”, with documentation at [retroui.dev](https://retroui.dev/docs). On 2026-09-25 the page title of retroui.dev began “NeoBrutalism — Retro UI components for React”.
Repository created 31 August 2024 under the GitHub organization “NeoBrutalism.com”. MIT License, copyright 2024 Arif Hossain.
observed: Heavy black condensed display type with a hard white-and-black offset, reading “Not every website has to look the same!”.
Mock browser windows with thick black frames, yellow title bars, and three-dot controls.
Cards inside the mock pages have black outlines and flat pastel or yellow fills.
Cartoon stickers (a yellow bird, cartoon eyes) have heavy black outlines.
interpretation: Shows the retro-window branch of the style that Malewicz and NN/g both describe: fake OS window chrome combined with outlines and hard shadows. The self-chosen name change to “Retro UI” also shows how close the neo-brutalist and retro-UI labels sit.
borrow: A window frame with a colored title bar is a cheap, recognizable container in this style. Use it for product demos, not for every card.

rights.statement: The repository is MIT-licensed, but the banner includes third-party logos (Figma, Tailwind CSS, React), so it is not stored here.
